parameters.content:
## Background Check + Risk Flags - Searchbug (api_ppl -> api_back)

Run a full background report on one person or a whole CSV of them. Every report is scored against what you actually searched, flagged for identity and financial risk, and written to three tabs: the report itself, the person's address history, and a one-row-per-person summary.

### How it works
1. **Single:** First Name, Last Name and State (Middle Name and City optional). **Bulk:** leave First Name blank and upload a CSV (first_name, last_name, middle_name, city, state).
2. Workflow Settings holds the tunable numbers (SSN masking, risk thresholds, candidate cap) so you retune the model without touching code. Validate Input drops rows missing a name or state; Dedupe Subjects removes repeat rows so you never pay for the same search twice.
3. **Two-step API:** People Search (api_ppl) finds the person and returns a reportToken, then Background Check (api_back) pulls the full report for that token. Both calls retry 3x and are throttled to 1 request/second.
4. Parse Report flattens the report; Score & Flag Match rates how well it matches the name and state you searched (MATCH_SCORE 0-100) and raises flags: SHARED_SSN, LIENS, MANY_ADDRESSES, NO_SSN_ON_FILE, WEAK_NAME_MATCH.
5. Three sheets are written:
   - **Background Check** - one row per report (29 columns, incl. MATCH_SCORE, RISK_LEVEL, FLAGS)
   - **BC Address History** - one row per address on file
   - **BC Summary** - one row per person searched: best match, risk level, combined flags, lien totals.

### How to set up
- [ ] Add your Searchbug CO_CODE + PASS in BOTH HTTP nodes
- [ ] Connect your OWN Google Sheets account in all three Save nodes
- [ ] Point them at your own spreadsheet and create three tabs:
      - "Background Check" (29 columns - see Save Report Detail)
      - "BC Address History" (13 columns - see Save Address History)
      - "BC Summary" (15 columns - see Save Subject Summary)
- [ ] Activate and share the form link

### Make it yours
- **Workflow Settings** (second node) - masking, risk thresholds, candidate cap.
- **Optional add-ons** (bottom of the canvas) - three unconnected, credential-free nodes you can plug in: a Webhook trigger for your CRM, a HIGH-risk filter, and a CSV export instead of Sheets.

### [!] Legal - FCRA
For informational use ONLY. NOT for employment, tenant, credit, or insurance screening. Searchbug data is not a consumer report under the FCRA.

### Privacy
SSNs are written masked (XXX-XX-1234). To store the full value, set MASK_SSN = false at the top of Parse Report - and make sure your sheet is locked down first.

### Risk logic
HIGH = someone else shares the SSN, or liens >= $10,000 - MEDIUM = any lien or 5+ addresses - LOW = neither.

## 1. Single or Bulk Input

Single or Bulk? checks whether the First Name field was filled. Single -> straight to Normalize Input; CSV upload -> Extract CSV first.

Normalize Input standardizes the column names (first_name / First Name / FIRST_NAME) so both paths share one schema.

Candidates Per Person controls how many possible matches to pull for each name - leave at 1 unless the name is common.

Workflow Settings sits between the form and this step, carrying the tunable thresholds into every Code node downstream.

## 2. Validate & Dedupe

Validate Input requires a first name, last name and state; anything else is logged as an invalid row instead of failing the run.

Dedupe Subjects then collapses repeat rows (same name + city + state) into one search and stamps each person with a SUBJECT_ID that follows them through both API calls and all three sheets.

## 3. Two-Step Searchbug Call

Searchbug needs two calls: People Search (api_ppl) returns a reportToken, then Background Check (api_back) exchanges that token for the full report.

Both nodes retry 3x and send 1 request per second, so a long CSV finishes instead of tripping rate limits. Check People Search routes names with no match to No Results Found.

Attach Subject Context carries the searched name and SUBJECT_ID past the first API call, and Extract Candidates makes one row per report token.

## 4. Parse, Score & Flag

Parse Report flattens the report into clean columns - names, DOB, addresses, phones, emails, relatives, businesses, shared SSNs and liens - and masks the SSN.

Score & Flag Match then rates each report against what you actually searched (MATCH_SCORE 0-100) and raises FLAGS. A low score means Searchbug returned a different person with a similar name - worth checking before you trust the row.

## [!] 5. Three Outputs

**Save Report Detail** - one row per report (29 columns).
**Save Address History** - one row per address on file, current first.
**Save Subject Summary** - one row per person searched: best match, highest risk level, combined flags, lien totals.

Connect your OWN Google Sheets credential in all three and create the tabs with matching row-1 headers.

Don't use the node menu's Refresh option - it erases the column mapping.

FCRA: informational use only - not for employment, tenant, credit, or insurance screening.

parameters.content:
## Optional add-ons - plug in what you need

These three nodes are deliberately left unconnected, and none of them needs a credential. Drag a connection to fit the workflow to your use case, or delete the ones you do not want.

- **[Optional] Webhook Trigger** - call the workflow from your CRM or app instead of the web form. POST first_name, last_name and state, then connect it into Normalize Input.
- **[Optional] Keep HIGH Risk Only** - insert after Score & Flag Match to carry on with the flagged subjects only.
- **[Optional] Export as CSV File** - hand the results back as a downloadable file instead of writing to Google Sheets.

Adding a Slack or email alert is the same idea: drop the node in after Keep HIGH Risk Only and connect your own account.

## Customize it here first

**Workflow Settings** holds every number the scoring uses:

- **max_candidates_cap** - hard ceiling on how many possible matches are pulled per name
- **mask_ssn** - true writes XXX-XX-1234, false writes the full SSN
- **risk_lien_threshold** - dollar amount that makes a lien HIGH risk (default 10000)
- **many_addresses_at** - how many addresses raise MANY_ADDRESSES (default 5)
- **weak_match_below** - MATCH_SCORE under this raises WEAK_NAME_MATCH (default 70)

Change them there and the whole workflow follows. You never need to open a Code node to retune the risk model.
